subject: Private deployment pairing: EU/APAC topology & egress control questions
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aimee Laurent <aimee.laurent@nordbank.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:15:00 +0200
Subject: Private deployment pairing: EU/APAC topology & egress control questions

Hi Aimee —

Great speaking earlier. To prepare a draft architecture and an initial security checklist for NordBank's private deployment, a few targeted clarifications would help us avoid rework:

- Residency expectation: we understand production data must remain in the EU primary region and APAC should be configured as a warm standby for disaster recovery. Can you confirm whether any subset of metadata (request IDs, routing keys) is allowed to be replicated to APAC, or must absolutely zero identifiable data cross the EU boundary?
- Failover model: do you want automatic failover (RTO oriented) or a manual activation with documented authorization? If manual, who is the approver and what is the acceptable activation window?
- Network/egress constraints: do you require a deny-by-default egress policy from APAC to any third-party endpoints, with explicit allow-lists for KMS and telemetry endpoints?
- KMS / key residency: will NordBank supply a regional KMS/HSM in EU and APAC, or do you prefer Redwood-managed key wrapping with customer-controlled KEKs?
- Compliance artifacts: if you can share the bank's security policy PDF and a short list of required artifacts (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, retention windows), we’ll map those to our private deploy controls.

I've attached a rough topology diagram we use for pairing exercises (jurisdictional_topology_v2.pdf) — it shows an active EU cluster with a warm APAC standby and example peering lines.

Next step proposal: once you confirm the bullets above, we’ll produce a short pairing proposal (network ports, BGP endpoints, expected latencies, and a proposed maintenance window) for sign-off.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai] [+1 415-555-0118]

[attachment: jurisdictional_topology_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Aimee Laurent <aimee.laurent@nordbank.eu>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private deployment pairing: EU/APAC topology & egress control questions

Thanks Jordan — good summary. Answers inline: 

- Residency: production customer data must remain within EU at rest and in transit. Non-identifiable telemetry (aggregated metrics) may be shared to APAC. No request/response payloads with customer IDs can leave the EU boundary.
- Failover: manual activation required for the first phase (we may move to automatic in a later iteration). Approver will be Head of ITOps (cc’d in this thread as our ITOps alias). Activation window: weekday maintenance window 01:00–05:00 UTC preferred.
- Egress: require deny-by-default from standby site with explicit allow-lists. KMS endpoints must be in-region; APAC standby should not be permitted to call EU KMS except as part of an authorized, logged failover.
- KMS: NordBank will provide regional KEKs (EU HSM). For APAC, we want the option to bring an HSM later — start with Redwood-managed key wrapping scoped to EU KEK policies.
- Compliance artifacts: attaching our security policy and a short list of required deliverables. Also need a BGP/peering contact and proposed ASN ranges for validation.

I'll loop in ITOps (itops@nordbank.eu) so they can validate peering.

Best,
Aimee
Head of Cloud Security — NordBank
[aimee.laurent@nordbank.eu]

[attachment: nordbank-security-policy.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aimee Laurent <aimee.laurent@nordbank.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, NordBank ITOps <itops@nordbank.eu>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private deployment pairing: EU/APAC topology & egress control questions

On Fri, 18 Jun 2027 at 14:02 +0200, Aimee Laurent <aimee.laurent@nordbank.eu> wrote:
> Thanks Jordan — good summary. Answers inline: 
> 
> - Residency: production customer data must remain within EU at rest and in transit. Non-identifiable telemetry (aggregated metrics) may be shared to APAC. No request/response payloads with customer IDs can leave the EU boundary.
> - Failover: manual activation required for the first phase ...

Thanks — that helps a lot. Marissa / Naomi — can you review the security asks below and confirm two technical points we’ll need to include in the pairing proposal: 

1) Sessions & KV cache: can we ensure per-tenant session affinity and ensure any cached KV material for a tenant is pinned to EU compute (no replication to APAC)? If not, we’ll propose a strategy that performs cache evacuation (invalidate/prefetch) as part of the manual failover flow.
2) Egress & peering: we will propose APAC standby with deny-by-default egress and a tightly scoped allow-list for telemetry and monitoring endpoints. We will also include explicit controls so APAC cannot contact EU KMS except during an audited failover; Naomi, what audit hooks do we provide for that path?

Proposed next deliverables (deliver by Tue 22 Jun):
- Short pairing proposal (ports, BGP endpoints, maintenance window, and peering checklist) — expected 2–3 pages.
- A matrix showing which artifacts NordBank requires for attestation and where Redwood can provide them (SOC2 extracts, audit logs, deployment evidence).

I’ll attach a draft PPT with the pairing concept.

Thanks,
Jordan

[attachment: private-pairing-proposal-1.pptx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aimee Laurent <aimee.laurent@nordbank.eu>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:18:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private deployment pairing: EU/APAC topology & egress control questions

Folks — quick security response and operational constraints we should capture in the proposal: 

- KV cache and session affinity: we can enforce tenant pinning to EU compute. Our runtime supports per-tenant routing rules and cache scoping; we will add a failover sequence that explicitly invalidates local caches and pre-warms EU caches before traffic is cut. That will be part of the runbook.
- KMS / HSM: initial model ok with Redwood-managed key wrapping scoped by EU KEK. We will instrument KMS calls with an immutable audit trail (request id, origin pod, timestamp) and stream those logs to a customer-controlled bucket/collector in EU. If NordBank brings an HSM in APAC later, we’ll require explicit config change and a documented authorization step.
- Egress lockdown: propose deny-by-default on standby, with only three allow entries: monitoring (aggregated metrics), Redwood health checks (aggregated), and the approved peering endpoints for coordination. No direct outbound calls to EU identity/KMS endpoints unless the manual failover runbook is executed and logged.
- Evidence & attestation: we can provide SOC2 extracts, runtime audit logs (TLS-terminated request traces), and a signed runbook with timestamps for each activation. For contract language, we recommend a clause covering manual failover authorization and a post-activation forensic package.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

(For NordBank ITOps: can you share the ASN ranges and a proposed /24 peering block so Marissa can draft the BGP matrix?)

From: Aimee Laurent <aimee.laurent@nordbank.eu>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, NordBank ITOps <itops@nordbank.eu>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private deployment pairing: EU/APAC topology & egress control questions

Thanks all — this aligns with our expectations. ITOps will provide ASN ranges and the primary peering contact.

Next operational step from our side: we can provide a 02:00–04:00 UTC maintenance window the week of Jun 28 to run a connectivity test (no data migration) and validate BGP reachability + egress allow-list enforcement on the APAC standby. Please include a single-slide runbook page that documents: 
- test objective;
- who authorizes the test;
- expected telemetry to collect;
- rollback criteria.

Once ITOps shares ASN details I’ll confirm the slot and we can proceed.

Regards,
Aimee
